reading.body:
The Flexential Salt Lake City - Fair Park facility publishes 22,539 square feet of technical space but no megawatt figure, making it impossible to estimate compute capacity or AI relevance from operator disclosures.

Certifications on the facility page—SOC 1 Type II, SOC 2 Type II, HITRUST CSF, and SSAE 18—indicate qualification for compliance-sensitive workloads in finance and healthcare rather than hyperscale training. These attestations define what can run there, not what does. The base isolation seismic design protects against earthquakes but does not indicate the power infrastructure or cooling capacity required for dense compute deployment.

Utah's 21 mapped data center facilities publish only 39 MW of capacity across three of them. This facility contributes zero to that figure. Without power disclosure from the operator, Fair Park remains unmeasurable as AI infrastructure. The pattern across the state suggests either small installations, private capacity held undisclosed, or both.
